title: 30-Year Treasury Bond auction (November refunding new issue) — 1:00pm ET, two hours after the same day's coupon announcement
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) and its text layer decompressed stream-by-stream. Row reads verbatim `30-Year BOND / Announcement Wednesday, November 04, 2026 / Auction Thursday, November 12, 2026 / Settlement Monday, November 16, 2026` — no trailing `R`, so a NEW ISSUE, announced by the 2026-11-04 quarterly refunding statement rather than by a coupon announcement. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon-auction convention and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-11-12 initial research (2026-09-08), sweeping that event's +/-5-day corridor. It earns a slot because it is the LARGEST duration event in its own proposer's session and the reason no reaction to that ~11:00 ET announcement will ever be attributable: this auction prices at 1:00pm ET the same day, alongside the 4-week and 8-week bill auctions, a 17-week bill auction displaced from Wednesday by the 2026-11-11 Veterans Day bond-market closure, the October Monthly Treasury Statement and Existing-Home Sales. It is also the first full bond session after that closure. EXPECTED SIZE, per the grid rather than per any current document: $25B. The 30Y new issue has printed $25B in every refunding month since 2024-02-08 (fiscaldata auctions_query, pulled 2026-09-08: 2026-02-12, 2026-05-13 and 2026-08-13 all $25B), and sb0590's own anticipated-size table reads 30-Year 25 in each of its two new-issue months (May-26, Aug-26). That number is NOT published for November today — sb0590's table ends at Oct-26 — and becomes published on 2026-11-04. THE STRUCTURAL NOTE this proposal carries: the November refunding block runs Mon 11-09 (3Y) / Tue 11-10 (10Y) / [Wed 11-11 closed] / Thu 11-12 (30Y), so a closed day sits inside a block that ran three consecutive business days in every other 2026 cycle. The 30Y is still the block's third auction, not a displaced one. The 3Y 11-09 and 10Y 11-10 legs were seen in the same parse and deliberately NOT filed here: they are sized and announced by treasury-refunding-2026-11-04, which this calendar already tracks and which is their natural owner, and filing a block of five auctions off one sweep would be noise rather than information. Proposed as an estimate; symbols: [] and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
